summary: Your 2001 Acura Integra has 168,000 miles on it and requires some important safety recalls and routine maintenance to stay reliable.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain replacement lamps were sold without amber side reflectors, which means other drivers might not see your car as well at night.
recalls.remedy_plain: AAI Motorsports will replace the noncompliant lamps for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain replacement headlights and marker lights were sold without amber side reflectors, reducing nighttime visibility.
recalls.remedy_plain: CK Motorsport will replace the noncompliant lamps for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain replacement corner lamps and headlights were sold without amber side reflectors.
recalls.remedy_plain: Pro-A Motors will offer to repurchase the noncompliant lamps.

recalls.summary_plain: Certain aftermarket headlights and corner lights were sold without required amber side reflectors.
recalls.remedy_plain: Tom Motorsport will offer reimbursement for the purchase of the lights.

recalls.summary_plain: Some passenger air bag modules were not properly welded and might fail to deploy in a crash.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will replace the passenger air bag module for free.

known_problems.explanation: Rubber components that grip the road and can wear down or lose pressure over time.
Safety cushions that inflate rapidly during a collision to protect passengers.
The group of parts that delivers power from the engine to the wheels.
The motor that powers the car, along with the system that keeps it from overheating.
The mechanism that allows you to control the direction the car travels.

maintenance_due.why: An internal rubber belt that synchronizes engine parts; if it snaps, the engine can be severely damaged.
Small devices that create the electrical spark to ignite fuel in the engine.
Fluid that flows through the engine to prevent it from overheating.
Hydraulic fluid that transfers pressure from your brake pedal to the brakes.
Special oil that lubricates moving parts inside the transmission, the gearbox that changes power speeds.

declined_services.risk_if_ignored: The belt can snap without warning and destroy the engine, requiring a full engine replacement.
Old fluid can cause internal transmission components to wear out and fail completely.
Low or degraded coolant can cause the engine to overheat and warp internal metal parts.
Old fluid absorbs moisture, which can lead to spongy brakes or total brake failure.
Worn plugs can cause poor fuel economy, engine misfires, and catalytic converter damage.

disclaimers: Costs and difficulty are estimates, not quotes.
Brakes, airbags, and fuel lines: have a professional check your work.
